name: Food For Thought
old_description: We just bought your Cherry Salsa and it is AMAZING! Can't wait to try your other products!
about:
Food For Thought operates from Traverse City, Michigan, where it runs a production kitchen and offices. The founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, nor are the founders named in available sources.

The company manufactures handcrafted, small-batch preserves, salsas, and sauces. Its product line includes items such as Cherry Salsa, Blueberry Lavender preserves, and Chipotle Ketchup, all produced in a dedicated production kitchen. Food For Thought also offers co-packing services and wholesale distribution for other brands.

The business serves retail consumers through direct online sales, as well as wholesale buyers and co-pack clients in the specialty food sector. Customer testimonials reference buyers from Michigan communities including Clinton Township, Northville, and Ann Arbor.

According to the company, its products are distinguished by clean ingredients and unique recipes that feature sophisticated flavor combinations, with an emphasis on letting customers taste the difference in every jar.

old_description: As one of Oregon State University's Agricultural Experiment Stations we provide technical, creative and educational service to food industry, entrepreneurs, and Northwest communities, with a focus on
about:
The Food Innovation Center operates in Portland, Oregon, as one of Oregon State University's Agricultural Experiment Stations. Established as a university-based service center, it provides technical, creative, and educational support to the food industry, entrepreneurs, and communities across the Northwest. The center houses the Western Regional Center to Enhance Food Safety (WRCEFS), one of four U.S. regional centers created to coordinate food safety training under the Food Safety Modernization Act.

The center delivers a range of services including product development and formulation from benchtop through pilot scale, shelf-life studies on finished products, nutrition labeling, sensory and consumer testing, and process authority services such as thermal process approvals. It also provides FSMA-focused training workshops for small and medium-sized farms, beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged farmers, and small processors. Consulting services cover economic analysis, community development, and market readiness research.

Clients span the food and beverage manufacturing sector, agricultural producers, and early-stage food entrepreneurs. The center works directly with small fresh fruit and vegetable merchant wholesalers, specialty food processors, and ingredient suppliers seeking formulation support or regulatory guidance. Its outreach extends to 13 western states and two territories through the WRCEFS sub-regional network.

The center was built to address gaps in food safety training and product commercialization for smaller operators. Its mission emphasizes quality, safety, and sustainability, aiming to reduce food waste and drive innovation funding across the regional supply chain.

name: Food Northwest
old_description: Version 2.0 is updated to reflect the FDA’s 2017 draft guidance, “
about:
Food Northwest operates from Portland, Oregon, where it was organized in 1914 as the Northwest Canners Association. Incorporated in Oregon in 1922, the trade association evolved through mergers and name changes — becoming the Northwest Food Processors Association in 1969 and rebranding as Food Northwest in 2018. The organization serves the food processing industry across Idaho, Oregon, and Washington from its office positioned midway between the three state capitals.

The association provides advocacy, training, technical resources, and networking for 350-plus member companies. Its professional staff manages government relations on food policy, environmental regulation, energy, and workforce issues; develops tools such as the Listeria Control Checklist and Sanitary Design Guide; and produces the annual Food Northwest Process & Packaging Expo, which marked its 50th edition in 2022. Five volunteer committees and task forces address sector-specific challenges, while the Education and Research Institute, incorporated in 2007, supports scholarships and workforce development.

Membership spans international brands, regional processors, and family-owned operations handling fruits, vegetables, seafood, dairy, bakery, specialty foods, and juices. Processor members represent nearly all food categories, while supplier members provide equipment, ingredients, and services to the industry. The association's Endowment Fund, established in 1989, funds food-science education at colleges in the three states.

Food Northwest was founded to advance the region's ability to produce and deliver safe, wholesome food to global markets. Its core priorities — food policy, government relations, environmental stewardship, energy, education, and sustainability — are set annually by the membership and affirmed by the Board of Directors, positioning the association as an authoritative voice for the Pacific Northwest food processing cluster.

name: Food Tech
old_description: Food Tech specializes in the planning/ engineering/construction of food process plants and cold storage facilities.
about:
Food Tech, based in Rockland, Massachusetts, operates as a design-build firm specializing in food processing plants and cold storage facilities. The company is a subsidiary of EMCOR Group, Inc., a Fortune 500 mechanical and electrical construction leader. Bob Ross, P.E., serves as president.

The firm provides end-to-end services including facility planning, preconstruction, architecture, engineering, and construction management. It does not self-perform construction, instead managing competitive bidding among subcontractors. A notable project is a 190,000-square-foot cheese production facility capable of processing two million pounds of milk per day, featuring robotic packing and palletizing.

Food Tech serves dairy, fresh food, frozen food, USDA meat plants, and cold storage sectors. Its clients range from large publicly traded companies to smaller regional processors, distributors, retailers, and wholesalers. Offices in Boston and Milwaukee support a national footprint.

The company differentiates itself through a single-source design-build model that delivers a guaranteed maximum price early, returns savings from competitive bids, and maintains in-house architecture and engineering. Its safety program is described as award-winning and industry-leading.

name: Food Truck Builders of Phoenix
old_description: Stainless Steel Fabrication for Food Tucks & Commercial Kitchens
about:
Food Truck Builders of Phoenix operates from Glendale, Arizona, where it designs, fabricates, and sells custom mobile kitchens. The company focuses on food trucks, concession trailers, carts, and kiosks, along with stainless steel fabrication for commercial kitchens. No founding year or ownership details are disclosed in public materials.

The shop builds complete food trucks and trailers from the ground up, handling design, permits, blueprints, and custom stainless steel work such as exhaust hoods, cabinets, shelves, and holding tanks. It also sells and installs new and used NSF‑approved cooking equipment, refrigeration, exhaust systems, work tables, and sinks, and offers a rental program for kitchen equipment. Repair services cover commercial refrigeration, cooking gear, exhaust systems, trailers, electrical, plumbing, and AC, with a 24‑hour turnaround and parts stocked for major brands. Fire suppression inspection, installation, and repair are also provided.

Customers include food‑truck entrepreneurs, chefs, and mobile‑food vendors nationwide; the company notes its units operate across the country. It also serves brick‑and‑mortar restaurants needing stainless steel fabrication or equipment. The business caters to both new builds and remodels of existing trucks.

The company differentiates itself by guaranteeing that every truck and trailer passes initial health inspections in any city or state, beating competitors' written quotes by 10%, and offering seller financing at 0% interest for 12 months with half down. Its repair experience informs equipment selection, ensuring compatibility in the tight confines of a mobile kitchen.

name: Food Truck Headquarters USA
about:
Food Truck Headquarters USA operates from Clinton Township, Michigan, serving as an online specialist for food‑truck kitchen equipment and appliances. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or the names of its founders.

The business stocks a curated selection of commercial‑grade equipment from brands such as Cookshack commercial smokers and Brood nitro coffee machines, targeting the specific spatial and power constraints of mobile and commissary kitchens. It functions as a distributor rather than a manufacturer, managing inventory, order fulfillment, and free shipping on most items, while explicitly stating it does not provide on‑site installation.

Its customer base consists of food‑truck entrepreneurs, food‑trailer and food‑cart operators, and commissary‑kitchen managers. The company’s educational content — covering topics from generator sizing to menu pricing — is aimed at both startup and established mobile‑food businesses across multiple states.

Food Truck Headquarters USA differentiates itself through hands‑on industry experience: its staff have built and operated food trucks, trailers, and commissary kitchens, allowing them to advise on equipment fit and functionality. The firm also publishes a library of how‑to guides and product comparisons to help buyers make informed purchasing decisions.

old_description: Our experienced consultants will help you start a food truck business plan. Learn the full rundown of how you can make a profit while managing costs.
about:
Food Trucks Northwest operates from Seattle, Washington, where founder Nick Parisi drew on more than 30 years of running his own mobile kitchen to launch a consultancy and fabrication shop. Parisi started the business after recognizing that new operators faced a maze of regulations, design choices, and operational pitfalls he had navigated alone.

The company designs and builds custom food trucks tailored to each cuisine, fabricating units that meet both road-legal and health-department standards. It also maintains a lineup of pre-built trucks for operators who want to launch quickly, and it provides consulting on business planning, cost management, and Washington Labor Industries compliance. No facility size or headcount figures are disclosed.

Clients range from first-time entrepreneurs to established restaurants and catering companies adding a mobile unit. The firm cites restaurant and catering businesses as typical customers seeking to expand revenue through on-site catering and street vending.

Parisi frames the service as a guided tour that helps owners avoid the headaches he encountered, emphasizing that every truck is engineered around the specific menu and workflow rather than a one-size-fits-all template. The company also promotes a fast-tracked path to state legalization, positioning its compliance guidance as a way to prevent fines and delays.

about:
FoodPrep Solutions operates from its headquarters in Stamford, Connecticut. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year or ownership structure, and no founders are named in available materials.

The business provides an all-in-one service for food-service operations, combining weekly or biweekly knife sharpening and exchange with food equipment sales, maintenance, and merchandise. Its sharpening programs cover commercial knives, grinder knives, can openers, plates, bowl choppers, HCM and VCM blades, and slicer or food-processor blades. The company states it supplies 100 percent of the knives in its exchange program, eliminating customer purchases, and serves accounts ranging from independent groceries to national chains.

FoodPrep Solutions targets restaurants, delis, bakeries, supermarkets, food-processing plants, and food-service management companies. Its client examples include mom-and-pop groceries, nationwide chains, and top food-service management firms that rely on the firm for sharpening, equipment, maintenance, and merchandise.

The company emphasizes its Kosher sharpening solutions under the highest level of rabbinical supervision as a key differentiator, along with a single-source model that bundles sharpening, equipment, maintenance, and merchandise to reduce vendor count.

name: Form Plastics Company
old_description: Form Plastics is a leading USA manufacturer of high-quality packaging solutions.
about:
Form Plastics Company is based in St. Charles, Illinois, and was founded in 1969. The company began by manufacturing custom thermoformed rigid plastic containers for food applications and has since expanded into a broader packaging solutions provider.

Today Form Plastics produces plastic and paper food trays, lidding and overwrap films that are converted and slit in-house, and a line of tray sealing machines ranging from manual to fully automatic models. The company also builds hinged paperboard sealing equipment and auxiliary packaging machinery, and supports customers with consulting, in-house CAD design, on-site training, and preventative maintenance programs.

Its primary customers operate in food service, school nutrition, and healthcare institutional dining, as well as non-food packaging markets. A testimonial from Richard Gray of TTS Machinery highlights the firm’s role in enabling domestic sourcing of packaging equipment.

Form Plastics emphasizes a “packaging with a purpose” philosophy, promoting eco-friendly materials and a start-to-finish Meal Packaging System for commissary operations. The company cites its solutions-management approach, reliability, and equipment contracts that require no capital outlay as key differentiators.

name: Formula Dynamics
old_description: Maintenance, repair, tuning, and upgrades for Ferrari, Maserati, Porsche, Lamborghini, McLaren, and the rest of the world's finest machines — backed by 20+ years of performance parts pedigree.
about:
Formula Dynamics operates from Las Vegas, Nevada, where it has run a performance parts business for over two decades before adding service bays. The company began as a specialist supplier of exhaust systems, tuning components, and genuine OEM parts for brands such as Ferrari, Maserati, and Lamborghini, eventually becoming the exclusive North American importer and distributor for Larini Systems exhausts. That parts pedigree led to the opening of a workshop that now handles maintenance, repair, tuning, and upgrades for the same exotic platforms.

The shop delivers factory-level service and performance work across nine makes — Ferrari, Maserati, Porsche, Lamborghini, McLaren, Aston Martin, Mercedes, Bentley, Rolls-Royce, and Audi. Capabilities include exhaust fitting and valve-controller setup, ECU and dyno tuning with baseline documentation, big-brake and carbon-ceramic servicing, forged-wheel sourcing with touchless mounting and road-force balancing, coilover installation with corner-weighting and alignment, dry-ice blasting for underbody and engine-bay restoration, paint correction, ceramic coating, and paint-protection film, plus turbo-system integration with supporting fueling and cooling hardware. A dyno cell, touchless tire equipment, and dry-ice blasting gear support the work, while the parts store continues to ship components worldwide.

Customers range from daily drivers to track-day participants and collectors who need documented service histories. The parts division supplies owners and independent shops globally with platform-correct exhausts, suspension, and tuning hardware.

The company says its differentiator is a “baseline first, platform correct, prove the result” discipline: every car receives a health check before modifications, all fluids and torque specs follow manufacturer procedures, and dyno sheets plus road tests verify the outcome. Membership at Spring Mountain Motorsports Ranch provides track validation for parts and setups. Because parts sourcing, installation, and calibration share one roof, the shop avoids finger-pointing between supplier and installer, and it maintains documentation to collector standards for each vehicle’s history file.
